result.title: Pretraining and Test-Time Training Budgets Matter for ARC: A Controlled Study of VARC and TRM
result.summary: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) is increasingly used to evaluate whether neural networks can infer task-specific transformations from few demonstrations. Recent ARC models differ in architecture, but also in broader training and evaluation protocols, including pretraining data, data augmentation, test-time setup, and optimization budgets, making conclusions about architecture benefits debatable. In this work, we study how the performance of the vision-inspired VARC and recursion-based TRM models is affected by pretraining and test-time training (TTT) budgets under a common inductive protocol on ARC-AGI-1. We cross five pretraining budgets with four TTT budgets for each test task. Each budget specifies a task-variant count and total sample presentations, defining the controlled training budgets. We observe that increasing TTT sample presentations improves the standard ARC pass@2 metric in all settings for both models. Increasing the TTT task-variant count consistently helps only TRM, whereas VARC often performs better with fewer variants. VARC also remains competitive without pretraining, while TRM benefits much more from it. These results show that pretraining and TTT budgets affect ARC evaluation and motivate reporting at comparable budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 ARC-AGI-1 上以统一归纳协议，将五种预训练预算与四种测试时训练（TTT）预算交叉，比较 vision-inspired 的 VARC 与递归式 TRM；结果显示增加 TTT 样本呈现量普遍提升 pass@2，任务变体数增加只稳定帮助 TRM，并据此主张在可比预算下报告结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其控制预算以区分架构与训练/测试时算力贡献的做法，可能为 LVR 中测试时计算成本、贡献归因与评测可比性提供方法线索；但研究对象是网格抽象推理，未涉及多模态 latent 状态，需核查可迁移程度。
